verse.reading: Making the mind a bow, the sky's spark its string and my awareness the arrow, when will I shoot?
verse.nuance: The bow is the Mundaka Upanishad's (there Om is the bow and the self the arrow); here the mind is the bow and the target is not named. வான்பொறி, the spark of space, is taken by tradition as the inner light or the breath; the verse does not say.

finding.claim: People's minds wander nearly half their waking time, and they report being less happy while wandering than while focused.

verse.reading: Taking clay from a pit of filth and mixing the lump in a stream of blood, the vessel the clever potter makes is not worth even a dry stick; dance.
verse.nuance: The potter is the Lord or the father, the clay and blood the seed and the womb's blood; வறகோட்டுக்கும் ஆகாது, not worth a dry twig, is the body's price. The image is the Siddhars' and Tirumular's pot, with the making added.

finding.claim: A typical human body holds roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells, so the body is in large part a community of other organisms.

verse.reading: Above the Avyakrita who holds the eggs, above Hiranyagarbha who is Vishnu, above the lightning-bright Virat Purusha, above these there is consciousness.
verse.nuance: வியாகிருதன், இரணியகர்ப்பன் and விராட் புருடன் are the three cosmic selves of Vedanta, presiding over the universe's deep sleep, dream and waking; the kummi equates Hiranyagarbha with Vishnu. இண்டமுண்ட is garbled, perhaps அண்டமுண்ட (who swallowed the eggs). சைதன்னியம் (chaitanya), consciousness, is above all three and is named Brahman in 2611.

finding.claim: Orch-OR proposes that consciousness arises from quantum computations in neuronal microtubules ending in gravity-related collapse; it remains speculative and is disputed by most physicists and neuroscientists.

verse.reading: Join the stainless mind to the Thing that is seen, as a magnet draws iron and holds it; and in calm, like the pot and its rope, follow without wavering and dance.
verse.nuance: The two images differ: the magnet is attraction that needs no effort, the pot tied to its rope is a bond that does not slip. காட்சியான வஸ்து (the Thing that is seen) makes the object of meditation something already perceived.

finding.claim: People's minds wander nearly half their waking time, and they report being less happy while wandering than while focused.

verse.reading: In the street of the crown's middle, in the kind that remained, the fresh moon spreading and sporting; the lamp that is vermilion, the silence that is meditation, the silence that is bound: Sivayam passed beyond.
verse.nuance: உச்சி மத்தி, the middle of the crown, is the highest centre. ஒழிந்திருந்த சாதி, the kind or caste that remained, is odd; it may mean what is left when all else is gone. செச்சி (vermilion, or the plant of that name) and கச்சி are rhyme words whose sense I cannot fix. கடந்ததே, passed beyond, closes the chapter.

finding.claim: Meditation is associated with reduced activity in the default mode network and changed coupling between it and attention and control networks, with larger effects in experienced practitioners.

verse.reading: One can remain: there is no kalpa of plant or root; in the solitary Brahman, melting, with the mind subdued, as one looks the body itself became firm; not roaming in confusion, not talking sects, not consorting with wastrels, not keeping company with the ... , see the guru's feet and bow deeply.
verse.nuance: செடிபூடு கற்பமில்லை is the plainest rejection of herbal kalpa in the work, and stands against 2353 and the formulas from 2397. கோளர் is unclear (slanderers? the planets?).

finding.claim: Small randomised trials suggest ashwagandha lowers self-reported stress and anxiety, with low certainty of evidence.

verse.reading: Not wandering about killing and torturing firm-rooted lives and eating them, but thinking of them as my own life, when shall I complete my tapas?
verse.nuance: தன்னுயிர்போல் எண்ணி is the Kural's measure of compassion applied to the renouncer's diet; the stanza names killing, torturing and eating as one act. மன்னுயிர், the lives that abide, is also the Kural's word for living beings.

finding.claim: Loving-kindness and compassion meditation improve self-reported wellbeing and reduce distress in small to moderate degree.

verse.reading: After it has dried, take it, son, and set it devotedly in a kasaputa fire; let it cool, and when you take it out it is a sindhuram of the colour of the dawn sun; smear an atom of it on every drug and set them in the puta: the nine metals yield, and the whole art called vedai is in your hands.
verse.nuance: செந்தூரம் is the red calcined product of Siddha chemistry; நவலோகம் the nine metals; the claim is a universal agent that transmutes. நீருமடா may mean the metals turn to liquid or lose their nature. Read as history of a claim, not as a method.

finding.claim: A scoping review found 220 cases of heavy-metal poisoning, mostly lead and mercury, linked to Ayurvedic and Siddha preparations, with most analysed samples over permissible limits.

verse.reading: When will the ruinous maya go and cease? When will the scattered mind come straight? When will I stand free of the infatuation that joins the woman with sword-like eyes? Mind, alas! When will all the desire for this hard world be cut at the root? Leaving the planet-like instruments you keep thinking on, look upward; and what it is that joins there, look at the root to see.
verse.nuance: Each எப்போ (when) is addressed to the mind, in the manner of the Pattinathar and Pambatti laments. கருவி (instruments) is the Siddhanta word for the tattvas, and கோளான, planet-like, makes them fates that circle one. The answer given is a direction: மேலே நோக்கி, மூலம் பாரே, look up and look at the root, the mooladhara, which the next work (ch 84) takes up at length.

finding.claim: On the predictive-processing account, perception is the brain's best guess about the causes of sensory input, constantly corrected by prediction error.

tamil: பீற்றற் து ருத்தியைச் சோறிடுந் தோற்பையைப் பேசரிய
காற்றிற் பொதிந்த நிலையற்ற பாண்டத்தைக் காதல் செய்தே
verse.reading: The oozing body, the obscene shed, the torn bellows stuffed with flesh, the leather bag into which rice is put, the unspeakable, unstable pot filled with wind: the poet loved it, carried it about and wandered.
verse.nuance: Five names for the body, each a container: a shed, a bellows, a bag, a pot. காற்றிற் பொதிந்த, packed with wind, names the breath as what the pot holds and what makes it unstable. The second and third agavals expand the catalogue to dozens of names.

finding.claim: A typical human body holds roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells, so the body is in large part a community of other organisms.

verse.reading: The washed clothes I change says 'I will not forget'; the rice pit, too, says 'I will not yet be filled'.
verse.nuance: சோற்றுக்குழி, the pit for rice, is the belly, and தூரேன் (I will not be filled in) is said of a pit. Fine laundered clothes and food are the body's own desires, after the mind's in 438 to 442.

finding.claim: The gut microbiota signals to the brain through immune, endocrine and vagal routes and affects stress responses and behaviour in animals; human causal evidence is still limited.

verse.reading: They do not know how to bind the alkali; without turning the fierce essence into calx, by joining veesam with camphor, is it not all in vain, girl?
verse.nuance: காரம், சாரம், நீறு and பூரம் are terms of Siddha chemistry: alkali, a salt or essence (sal ammoniac in some lists), calcined powder, and camphor or borax. வீசம் is unidentified, perhaps a measure or a substance. The verse argues the order of operations matters and the ignorant skip the binding step.

finding.claim: Mercury can be turned into gold only by nuclear reactions such as neutron bombardment of mercury isotopes, never by chemical or alchemical processing.

verse.reading: The beginningless mantra that is five and three and is not reached: if you think of it in your heart and recite it until you take its form, even a hundred crore of the five great sins fly off like cotton, so the four Vedas declare.
verse.nuance: அஞ்சும் மூணும் எட்டாதாய் puns on எட்டு: five and three make eight, and the mantra is 'unreachable'. Tradition reads the eight as the five letters with the three of Om, or as an eight-syllable mantra. நீருருச் செபிப்பீரேல் may be 'recite till you become it' or 'recite (while) you are water' (that is, at bathing). Compare 1022, which again joins five and three in one letter.

finding.claim: The idea that a fixed stock of breaths or heartbeats sets lifespan rests on a cross-species correlation; within humans, lower resting heart rate predicts lower mortality but slowing breath has not been shown to extend life.

verse.reading: In the first cause the body does not age. Fold the tongue back toward the nose, go up by the channel of sound, and if you can hold the pair pressed hard with longing cut away, then look and look and every direction becomes the supreme Brahman.
verse.nuance: The tongue folded toward the nose is the khechari seal; நாத நாடி, the channel of sound, is the central channel. இரட்டை (the pair) is unexplained, in tradition the in- and out-breaths or the two side channels, and ஏக்கறுத்து may be 'cutting longing' or a form of ஏக்கம் (panting). The first line's claim that the body does not age at the source is the Siddhars' deathlessness, stated as a condition reached by the practice.

finding.claim: Reciting a rosary prayer or a yoga mantra slows breathing to about six a minute and raises baroreflex sensitivity, linking repetitive recitation to the slow-breath physiology.

verse.reading: Thandavakkona, discern and know that the nature of this pot of a body is in truth that of a jar of filth.
verse.nuance: கடம் is the pot and சால் the jar: the body is a vessel and what it holds is மலம், excrement, here in its plain sense rather than the three impurities. The line is a standard renouncer's image put in the herdsman's mouth.

finding.claim: A typical human body holds roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells, so the body is in large part a community of other organisms.

verse.reading: As they began, subduing the mind and guarding their state, standing pure and at play, he saw the audacity of the asuras whose minds would not be subdued, who made trouble without fear; firmly he mounted the peacock, took the red vel, meditated on its point so that the reddened asura kin should die, and loosed it, and the asura kin flew away.
verse.nuance: அடங்கி மனம் அடங்காத அசுரர் sets the sages' subdued mind against the asuras' unsubdued one in a single phrase, the nearest the narrative comes to saying what the asuras are. The vel is loosed by meditation on its point (தியானம் பண்ணி), not by the arm.

finding.claim: People's minds wander nearly half their waking time, and they report being less happy while wandering than while focused.

verse.reading: When will I have died already, before the soul in its cage falls dead, slowly, as with a yawn?
verse.nuance: கூண்டு, the cage, is the body; the yawn (கொட்டாவி) is the slow last breath. To die before dying is the Siddhar's state of the living dead, the self already gone while the body stands, taken up again at 90, 126 and 139.

finding.claim: A typical human body holds roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells, so the body is in large part a community of other organisms.

verse.reading: They do not see the key of alchemy, nor perceive the drug of the five elements; why do they blow smoke through the tube? Ask what this is, girl of knowledge.
verse.nuance: The திறவுகோல் (key) of vaadham is what the kummi will say is inward; பஞ்சபூதச் சரக்கு, the drug of the five elements, can be read as an actual mineral set or as the five elements of the body. குழல் புகை ஊதுதல், blowing fumes through the blowpipe, is the outward craft being mocked.

finding.claim: About one in five Ayurvedic products bought online in the US contained detectable lead, mercury or arsenic, including rasa shastra metal preparations.

verse.reading: You devotees who keep saying 'the five letters and the three letters': the thing itself is neither the five letters nor the three. Press the five letters into the heart and know that letter, and the five letters take on the colour of that: Sivayam.
verse.nuance: The mantra is denied as the goal and kept as the means: the five pressed into the heart (நெஞ்சழுத்து) lead to 'that letter' (அவ்வெழுத்து), which is unnamed, and then the five become its colour. The three letters are அ உ ம, the parts of Om. The stanza is the poet's own gloss on his refrain: Sivayam is not the syllables.

finding.claim: Silent repetition of a single word reduces activity widely across the cortex, including default-mode regions, compared with rest.

verse.reading: You build long houses and shut tall doors; is it because you want to live, rejoicing people? When the sound of Death comes, all stand with hands wrung; the feet of the one who ate the poison and the feet of the Mother are the truth.
verse.nuance: கைகலந்து நின்றிடும் can be hands joined in helpless appeal or kin standing mingled in grief. The oath line closes as at 968.

finding.claim: Fasting strongly induces autophagy in animal tissues, but direct evidence that it does so in human tissues is sparse.

verse.reading: All the honey that came with the bee and the flower's scents is eaten and subsides within; in that manner, reciting with the root of the linga, if you can see and see and make thought subside at the root, the strong deeds taken on of old fly away: Sivaayame.
verse.nuance: The honey drawn in and settled is the figure for attention drawn to the root (வேர்); லிங்க மூலம் may be the root centre or the base of the inner linga. The verse's claim is that old deeds leave when thought settles there.

finding.claim: On the predictive-processing account, perception is the brain's best guess about the causes of sensory input, constantly corrected by prediction error.

verse.reading: Can this worldly life be given up? Having given it up, can the mind grow firm? Without your grace, can the daily wandering be crossed? Must I go to the gates of the petty and suffer with tears welling? Sokkanatha, Sundara Pandya.
verse.nuance: The questions of the first three lines are answered by the third's condition: none of it is possible without grace. The fourth line, standing at the door of the petty, is the fate the poet fears for one who leaves the world without grace, the same begging from the rich that 325 refuses. Sundara Pandya is Siva as the Pandya king of Madurai.

finding.claim: Expectation and conditioning engage opioid, dopamine and prefrontal systems to produce real changes in pain and symptoms, chiefly in subjective outcomes.

verse.reading: A horse that cannot be reached, with twelve legs, a burden even when let go: if I stop it in the street, take a rope and bind all four legs tight, could I not rule all the eight-sided land, my Mother?
verse.nuance: The horse is the breath in Siddhar cipher; its twelve legs are the twelve finger-breadths the breath travels, or the twelve kalas. Binding its four legs is holding the breath, and ruling the eight-sided country (அட்டாள தேசம்) is the sovereignty of the eight siddhis, or of the eight directions. The verse is a single image kept in question form.

finding.claim: Breathing voluntarily at about six breaths a minute raises vagally mediated heart-rate variability during practice, right after one session and after multi-session training.

verse.reading: The hero tells the golden girl, like Thiruvekambam of the Lord who holds the firm Ganga on his locks, that if the forest men come with their eagle-strong force, his hot boar-like arrows will make them prey for the wing-spreading eagles, and that if he has his firm striped bow he will not hide.
verse.nuance: பருந்து (eagle) is repeated in every line, and வெய்யேனம் may be a hot boar or a fierce arrow; the sense is the hero's reassurance on the robber-infested road. மறைகுவனே at the close is odd as a boast; it may be 'I will not hide' with a lost negative, or 'I will take cover'.

finding.claim: Case reports document severe poisoning, including cerebral edema, from Siddha capsules containing arsenic, mercury and lead thousands of times above safe limits.

verse.reading: The letter is the letter of silence; if so, it is the good key; if one opens with it so as to free, the way to the crown is seen, jnana girl.
verse.nuance: The key to the locked gate is a mantra that is not spoken: மௌனாக்ஷரம், the silent letter, which tradition identifies with the unuttered Om or the ajapa breath. முத்திதமாக is read as 'so as to release'. உச்சி வழி, the way to the crown, is the goal the key opens.

finding.claim: Silent repetition of a single word reduces activity widely across the cortex, including default-mode regions, compared with rest.

verse.reading: When will I leave ignorance, touch the limit of grace-knowledge, gain the house of true knowledge and come forth?
verse.nuance: Three stages are named in order: அஞ்ஞானம், அருள் ஞானம், மெய்ஞ்ஞானம், with grace-knowledge as a stage that has a limit (எல்லை) to be touched and passed. மெய்ஞ்ஞான வீடு gives the work its title; வெளிப்படுவது is to emerge or be revealed, the poet's own coming out into the open.

finding.claim: Placebos given openly, with patients told they are inert, still produce moderate improvements in self-reported symptoms.

verse.reading: In the bewilderment that women with collyrium-dark eyes cast, you have lost yourselves; if you would be free of trouble, and if by a mind that has known truth you gain the knowledge that shines, you will know how to be saved and live for aeons.
verse.nuance: ஐயிறந்து is read as ஐயம் இறந்து (doubt gone) or ஐ இறந்து (having lost the self, or having passed the five). ஊழிகாலம் வாழ்வீர், living for aeons, is the Siddhar claim of a deathless body, or long life by knowledge; the verse does not separate the two.

finding.claim: Quantum cognition uses the mathematics of quantum probability to model order effects and violations of classical probability in human judgment; it makes no claim that brains are quantum devices.

verse.reading: Having bought it, join the brain in the egg and mix in the leaf richly, son; set it inside a twisted spurge, closing the mouth of the hollow and removing the curse; when three months have gone, take out the spurge and, doing no more rite, make a seal of cloth and clay and dry it.
verse.nuance: The verse is an alchemical procedure read here for what it claims: a preparation of salt and some substance sealed in a கள்ளி (spurge) for three months, then sealed with cloth and clay for firing. அண்டத்தில் மூளை (brain in the egg, perhaps an eggshell, perhaps a skull) and வப்பிலை are unclear. சாபந் தீர்த்தே, removing the curse, is the alchemist's word for purifying a substance.

finding.claim: Case reports document severe poisoning, including cerebral edema, from Siddha capsules containing arsenic, mercury and lead thousands of times above safe limits.

verse.reading: We will shut the snake in the pot of ம, we have scooped up and eaten the breath of the jewelled circle, we will push away the pots of வ, leap past the crooked dream, let it dance in the open sea of space, offer the five instruments as sacrifice, and saying we stand become the form of சி, see the holy feet, be clear and dance.
verse.nuance: The letters are those of the five-letter mantra: in the usual Saiva reading ம stands for mala or the body, வ for grace, சி for Siva. The snake begins in ம and ends as சி, so the stanza is a passage through நமசிவாய from bond to Siva. பஞ்ச கருவி are the five senses, and வாசி is the breath as practice.

finding.claim: Reciting a rosary prayer or a yoga mantra slows breathing to about six a minute and raises baroreflex sensitivity, linking repetitive recitation to the slow-breath physiology.

verse.reading: When the pure supreme space itself appeared as light, the poet gained the joy of true knowledge; on beholding Being, Consciousness and Bliss, that all is pervaded by Brahman is hard to put into words.
verse.nuance: சகலமும் பிரமமயம் is the Advaitic formula, rare in the earlier Siddhars and common in the later Vedantic ones. புகலரிதே, 'hard to tell', repeats the disclaimer of 2297.

finding.claim: Orch-OR proposes that consciousness arises from quantum computations in neuronal microtubules ending in gravity-related collapse; it remains speculative and is disputed by most physicists and neuroscientists.

verse.reading: As the sun and moon in the sky grew and then became one, the poet says he does not know the breathing of life within the fleshly body.
verse.nuance: கதிர் மதி, sun and moon, are the two breaths in Siddhar cipher, and their growing and becoming one is their joining in the middle channel, as tradition reads; the plain reading, that the sky's two lights become one (at new moon, or in eclipse), gives the simile its surface. உயிர்ப்பு is the breathing itself, the one practice the whole litany names directly.

finding.claim: Claims that breathing through one nostril selectively activates the opposite brain hemisphere or shifts sympathetic versus parasympathetic tone rest on small, inconsistent studies.

verse.reading: Just be still, demon; I have told you the formula. The place where you stayed still is what was pointed to.
verse.nuance: சும்மா இரு (simply be, do nothing) is the work's one positive instruction, called a சூத்திரம் in mockery of the sutras rejected in 1674. சுட்டது is from சுட்டு (to point out) or சுடு (to burn); the stillness is either the thing indicated or the thing that burns away the rest. 1686 and 1690 repeat it.

finding.claim: Meditation is associated with reduced activity in the default mode network and changed coupling between it and attention and control networks, with larger effects in experienced practitioners.

verse.reading: In the tank of Kayampatti the white kasa root has sprouted; if one rises upright from the mouth-river, the body will not perish, girl of knowledge.
verse.nuance: காயாம்பட்டி reads as the 'village of the body' (காயம்), its tank a bodily place; காசாம் வேர், the root of the kasa (white-flowered) plant, is a herb or its cipher. வாயாற்றினின்று நிமிர்ந்தால், rising from the river of the mouth, may point to the turning of breath or nectar upward. The claim is the kalpa claim of an undying body, here located within.

finding.claim: Small randomised trials suggest ashwagandha lowers self-reported stress and anxiety, with low certainty of evidence.

verse.reading: The poet asks what it matters however much one has learned or whatever one has gained, and whether those who do not know you will be saved.
verse.nuance: கற்றால் என், பெற்றால் என், what if learned, what if gained: learning and possessions are set together as things that do not save, so the chapter's attack on learning is an extension of chapter 39's on wealth. உய்வரோ, will they be saved, is a question with its answer in it.

finding.claim: On the predictive-processing account, perception is the brain's best guess about the causes of sensory input, constantly corrected by prediction error.

verse.reading: The desire for land has had me eaten by land; the desire for gold and the desire for women say 'I will not go'.
verse.nuance: The three desires, மண், பொன், பெண், are the standard Tamil triad (மூவாசை). மண்ணுண்டு போட்டது is a pun: land eaten the lover of land, as the earth eats the buried. From here to 447 each desire is made to speak in the first person, என்குதே, so the poet's will is shown as not his own.

finding.claim: People adapt to most gains and losses so that happiness drifts back toward a personal set point, though not fully for every life event.

verse.reading: Whatever work they do, whatever hardship they undergo, the minds of the freed stay in silence; skilfully, like the servant woman who comes playing and swinging both her arms as she walks, her mind is on the water pot on her head.
verse.nuance: The figure of the water carrier is exact: the body is free to move and play because the attention is fixed elsewhere, and the pot does not fall. The verse frees the jnani's outer life from any required form, work or austerity, and so stands against the ascetic marks the poet himself lists elsewhere (357, 360); what is required is only where the mind is.

finding.claim: Meditation is associated with reduced activity in the default mode network and changed coupling between it and attention and control networks, with larger effects in experienced practitioners.

verse.reading: Dogs who say 'jnani, jnani', millions upon millions; disputants who talk of a rainy day with no sky, millions upon millions; fools who do not see the nature of the selfless ocean say 'we knew it before' without ..., millions upon millions.
verse.nuance: வானிலாத மழைநாள், a rainy day without a sky, is an impossibility, so the disputants argue about nothing. தானிலா சாகரம், the ocean without self, is the state they cannot see. மூனிலாமல் is unknown to me; முன்னறிந்த may be the boast of prior knowledge or of knowing the First.

finding.claim: People's minds wander nearly half their waking time, and they report being less happy while wandering than while focused.

verse.reading: Making the sky a bow and the five letters an arrow, mounting the chariot of mantra to hunt the deer, in the grove where the moon and sun have gone, will I not come and play and look with a glad mind, my Mother?
verse.nuance: The deer hunt is the chase of the restless mind (மான் as deer and as the mind). Sun and moon are the two breaths in Siddhar cipher; the grove where they have gone is where the two channels end and the central one opens. The five letters are the Siva mantra.

finding.claim: The body replaces around 330 billion cells a day, mostly blood and gut cells, so its material is continually renewed.

verse.reading: The stinking body, the bundle of rice for foxes, the pot the poet fills daily with rice and curry: grant, he asks, that it not fall into the pit from which women's filth and blood flow, but climb out.
verse.nuance: The petition answers 250, where the poet said he could not see the bank to climb; here he asks for the climbing (ஏறும்படி). The body and the woman are both described by what flows into and out of them, rice into one, filth from the other.

finding.claim: A typical human body holds roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells, so the body is in large part a community of other organisms.

verse.reading: Look: rising at dawn, without hurry set the mind at the suzhumunai; when the sun and moon exchange and rise at the suzhumunai that is the womb, standing within the uvula without wavering, see it subside within the suzhumunai; of the sixteen, the eight and the four and the three, without scattering, join as one and go.
verse.nuance: பரிதிமதி, the sun and moon, are the right and left breaths in the Siddhars' cipher, and their exchange at the central channel is the practice; a plain reading, that sunrise is the hour, is also present in உதயத்தில் எழுந்திருந்து. கருவான சுழுமுனை, the suzhumunai that is the womb or seed, repeats the run's link between the yogic centre and conception. The arithmetic of sixteen, eight, four and three is from 2432.

finding.claim: Meta-analysis of small randomised trials finds alternate-nostril breathing lowers blood pressure modestly, with high heterogeneity between studies.
